Looping in the infra run team notes from the sandbox run and next-test plan: 

Sandbox test notes (run id: run-nx-20270212-01):
- Model: openchat-7b-v2-quant (quantization config q4_0 for embeddings, q8_0 for attention kernels).
- HW: 8x A100-40GB per test harness node (we pinned to a single 8-GPU pool to simulate Dedicated).
- Test harness: internal jmeter variant + custom token-producer that simulates clinician typing cadence and variable prompt length (median 85 tokens).
- Warmup: 1200 requests to populate KV cache and test prefix reuse.
- Observation: a cold-start run (no KV warmup) showed p95 TTFT ~1.1s; warm cache reduced p95 to 530ms (gain ~52%).
- Batching: batch=4 gave best throughput/latency balance; batch=1 improved TTFT p50 by ~40ms but reduced aggregate throughput by ~20%.
- Concurrency stress: 60 concurrent sessions (synthetic) pushed p95 TTFT to ~1.4s on the 8-GPU pool; with autoscale cushion (+25% capacity) the expected p95 drops below 800ms.

Next tests scheduled:
- Wed 2027-02-17: 60-concurrency canary (production-like prompt set). Collect GC/memory traces and full p50/p95/p99 breakdowns.
- Thu 2027-02-18: Variant run with batch=2 and KV-prefetch to measure TTFT improvement at cost of throughput.

I’ll attach the raw traces and a short script to parse the per-token latency buckets.

- Aditya
